recognition.note: Two rival governments. This card is the internationally recognised Government of National Unity in Tripoli (prime minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah), listed by the United Nations as Libya's government. The House of Representatives voted on 13 Aug 2024 to end its term and backs a rival Government of National Stability in Benghazi (the Hammad government), whose military arm is Khalifa Haftar's Libyan National Army; Haftar's camp holds most of the oilfields. The eastern authority has no actor of its own in the atlas: it is recorded through this card's objectives, constraints and actions, and through the other cards that deal with it.

objectives.text: Remain the sole UN-recognised government, and in office, until an election on terms Dbeibah can survive. The GNU was installed through a UN process in 2021 for elections that were set for December 2021 and never held; the House of Representatives voted on 13 Aug 2024 to end its term and appointed a rival government in Benghazi, yet the UN protocol list still names Dbeibah as prime minister, and he stayed in office after thousands demanded his resignation on 16 May 2025.

grand_strategy.reading: Libya is a state whose two halves are each a client, and the card of the recognised half has to be read as the card of a client that holds the title deeds. Tripoli has the United Nations list, a Turkish shield, the Central Bank and the Italian gas contract; Benghazi has the oilfields, the army, Russian air bases at six sites, the Emirati air bridge to Kufra and the Egyptian border. Luttwak's relational manoeuvre turns on seams between an opponent and its allies, and here the seams are in the patrons themselves: Turkey backs Tripoli and courts Haftar's son, Egypt trains the east's officers and sends its intelligence chief to Dbeibah, Italy and Greece pay both coasts, and Washington brokers a unified budget and a power-sharing scheme that would make Saddam Haftar president. Every patron has a reason to keep the division manageable and none to end it: a united Libya would answer to one capital, and each of them has a deal with a different one. The 2026 state is a stalemate that is eroding - a unified budget (11 Apr), a Tripoli agreement on an elections commission and a single executive (30 Aug), a House that endorsed it and a High Council that did not, UNSMIL's mandate up for renewal on 31 Oct, new fighting in Zawiya - and the paradox of the card is that Dbeibah's best moves (purging the militias, courting Washington, selling Europe departures) each work for the east as well or better, so Tripoli's strength is its recognition, which is the one asset the UN process is designed to retire.
